D-01.scope: Production web, API, identity login, and worker-backed core business journeys
exclusions: Client-network failures before the AWS edge
D-01.errorBudgetPolicy: At 50% consumption stop discretionary releases; at 100% freeze all non-remediation releases pending incident review; scheduled maintenance and AWS regional failures consume the budget

D-02.recoveryScope: Coordinated recovery of application PostgreSQL, Keycloak PostgreSQL and realm, and object storage
D-02.completeSetDefinition: A checksummed application PostgreSQL, Keycloak PostgreSQL and realm, and object-storage set copied to an approved target in a separate failure domain, encrypted with an independently approved backup KMS key, remotely checksum-verified, and held under the approved immutable/versioned retention policy

D-03.legalHoldPolicy: Retain indefinitely without deletion or overwrite until written release jointly authorized by PRIVACY-OWNER and DATA-OWNER; statutory retention or active hold overrides privacy erasure

D-08.hostingModel: Self-managed on at least two RHEL 9 x86_64 Amazon EC2 nodes with OpenJDK 21 and a separate Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 18 Multi-AZ database
D-08.regionsAndHa: AWS ap-southeast-3 Jakarta; identity nodes in private subnets across separate Availability Zones; Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 18 Multi-AZ
D-08.supportTierAndSla: Red Hat Premium production support; 24x7 Severity 1/2; initial response 1 hour Sev1 and 2 hours Sev2, subject to executed subscription
D-08.patchCadence: Review vendor advisories daily; apply Critical/Important security fixes within 72 hours of supported release; apply other supported patches monthly after backup, smoke, and rollback validation
D-08.exitStrategy: Retain versioned realm exports, RDS backups, and the client/claim mapping; replacing Keycloak requires a superseding accepted ADR plus a tested OIDC cutover and rollback rehearsal
D-08.realmClientClaimContract: Keycloak OIDC Authorization Code with S256 PKCE; one-time database-backed authorization transactions; browser-bound state and nonce; RS256 ID-token verification through discovery/JWKS; profile synchronization; opaque server-side sessions; no access or refresh tokens persisted or exposed to the web application
D-08.mfaRecoveryBreakGlassContract: MFA required for privileged users; two individually named vaulted break-glass accounts; dual authorization; quarterly recovery test; rotate credentials after every use
D-08.keyRotationRevocationBackupContract: Rotate realm signing keys every 180 days with 30-day verification overlap, client secrets every 90 days, revoke immediately on compromise; encrypted daily realm export plus RDS backups included in coordinated recovery set

D-09.productAndTier: Amazon S3 Standard in ap-southeast-3 with cross-account cross-region replication to ap-southeast-1
D-09.accountRegionEndpoint: Primary production AWS account in ap-southeast-3 using https://s3.ap-southeast-3.amazonaws.com; cross-account replication target in ap-southeast-1
D-09.supportTierAndSla: AWS Basic Support; no production response-time SLA or MECO Flow application/identity operations ownership; subject to accepted R-12 and the paid-support procurement trigger
D-09.exitStrategy: Inventory and checksum every current object and version, export through the S3-compatible API, re-encrypt in the replacement store, reconcile metadata/object counts and checksums, and rehearse cutover and rollback
D-09.kmsAndPrivatePolicyContract: Private HTTPS S3-compatible storage with explicit aws:kms encryption and key ID, or AES256 only with evidence that SSE-S3 is backed by the approved external KMS; provider evidence must prove encrypted write/read, denial of unencrypted writes, anonymous-access denial, and versioning
D-09.retentionVersioningLegalHoldContract: Enable S3 Versioning and Object Lock with retention periods governed by D-03; legal holds suspend expiry; deny anonymous/public access, unencrypted writes, retention bypass, and unauthorized version deletion
D-09.malwareScanningContract: Objects remain quarantined until completion verifies metadata, size, SHA-256, detected type, and ClamAV result; disabled, unavailable, error, timeout, or malware detection remains SCAN_FAILED; only CLEAN review or approved versions may receive authorized short-lived downloads
D-09.replicationAndRecoveryContract: Copy the coordinated checksummed application PostgreSQL, Keycloak PostgreSQL and realm, and object-storage set to an approved target in a separate failure domain; encrypt with the independently approved backup KMS key, verify the remote checksum, apply approved immutable/versioned retention, and retain evidence of a clean restore rehearsal
